caption: Figure 11.4: 3D unstructured solvers: extruded triangular prisms (PrismFIT3D) versus general tetrahedra (UnstructuredFIT3D). Left: PrismMesh extrudes body-fitted 2D (x, y) triangles across independent 1D z layers z₀ < z₁ < … < z_K; the 2D Voronoi dual × 1D z dual keeps all 3D Hodge matrices strictly diagonal, while PolygonComplex2D (merge_tol=0.15) merges nearly cocircular triangle pairs into quadrilaterals to eliminate short Voronoi dual edges. Right: UnstructuredFIT3D discretizes e on tetrahedral edges and b on triangular faces, offering fast diagonal hodge='voronoi' (52 ns/tet/step) and unconditionally SPD hodge='whitney' (sparse LU via splu) when sliver tetrahedra have exterior circumcentres.
visual_intent:
Textbook-quality scientific schematic for a computational electromagnetics user manual. Flat vector style on a white background, high contrast, thin dark outlines, generous whitespace, sans-serif labels. Colour code used in every figure: primary grid G and its quantities in blue, dual grid G-tilde and its quantities in orange, exact/topological items in dark grey, approximate/material items in green, failure or warning items in red. Colourblind-safe. Every label must be spelled exactly as listed in this brief; mathematical symbols must be typeset correctly (hats, tildes, subscripts, transposes). Do not add any number, value, equation, software name, product name, logo, watermark or title that is not listed in this brief. Prefer fewer, larger labels over many small ones. No 3D photorealism, no cartoon characters, no hand-drawn or xkcd style.

Two equal panels side by side. LEFT PANEL headed '3D Extruded Prism FIT (PrismFIT3D)': Top half shows an isometric 3D triangular prism element (blue) formed by extruding a 2D (x, y) triangle across independent 1D z layers along a vertical axis 'z₀ < z₁ < … < z_K'. Inside the prism draw the orthogonal 2D Voronoi dual polygon in (x, y) extruded along the 1D z dual (orange), with a green badge '2D Voronoi dual × 1D z dual ⇒ all 3D Hodge matrices strictly diagonal (GPU acceleration)'. Bottom half inset titled 'PolygonComplex2D (merge_tol=0.15)': on the left, two nearly cocircular triangles sharing a diagonal edge with two circumcentres (orange dots) almost touching, connected by a tiny red dual edge labelled 'short Voronoi dual edge shrinks 3D CFL timestep'; an arrow 'merge' points to a single merged blue quadrilateral on the right with one clean central dual vertex (green check). Bottom note: '220 nm Si micro-ring: 15× fewer unknowns, 22× less work than Cart.; ~28× faster in wall time than 3D tets on rod cavity'. RIGHT PANEL headed '3D Tetrahedral FIT (UnstructuredFIT3D)': Top half shows a 3D tetrahedron (blue primal edges carrying electric voltages 'e' with arrows, shaded blue primal triangular face carrying magnetic flux 'b' pierced by an orange dual edge). Bottom half compares two cards: Card 1 'hodge="voronoi"': 'diagonal Delaunay–Voronoi Hodge, explicit leapfrog (52 ns/tet/step)', with a red warning sketch of a flat sliver tetrahedron whose orange circumcentre lies outside it ('sliver tetrahedron: negative dual entries'). Card 2 'hodge="whitney" (Bossavit & Kettunen 1999)': 'consistent non-diagonal Whitney 1-form / 2-form mass matrices, unconditionally SPD on slivers (sparse LU via splu, O(N_tet^1.5) memory)'.
target_diagram_desc0:
The figure is a textbook-quality scientific schematic designed for a computational electromagnetics user manual, featuring a flat vector style with a pure white background. It utilizes high contrast, thin dark outlines, and generous whitespace. All text is cleanly typeset in a legible sans-serif font. The diagram adheres to a strict, colorblind-safe coding system: the primary grid ($G$) and its quantities are blue, the dual grid ($\tilde{G}$) and its quantities are orange, exact/topological text and items are dark grey, approximate/material/success items are green, and failure/warning items are red.

The layout is divided evenly into two side-by-side vertical panels, separated by ample whitespace or a subtle thin grey divider.

**Left Panel: 3D Extruded Prism FIT (PrismFIT3D)**
*   **Header:** Positioned at the top in large, bold, dark grey sans-serif text is "3D Extruded Prism FIT (PrismFIT3D)".
*   **Top Half (Extruded Prism Schematic):** Displays an isometric 3D triangular prism. The primary edges of the prism are drawn in blue. A vertical axis runs alongside it, annotated in dark grey with the mathematical sequence "$z_0 < z_1 < \dots < z_K$". Inside the blue prism, the dual grid is illustrated in orange, depicting an orthogonal 2D Voronoi dual polygon in the $(x, y)$ plane that is extruded along the 1D $z$ dual axis. Positioned adjacent to this geometric drawing is a rounded rectangular green badge containing the text: "2D Voronoi dual × 1D z dual ⇒ all 3D Hodge matrices strictly diagonal (GPU acceleration)".
*   **Bottom Half Inset (Merging Diagram):** A boxed or demarcated subsection titled "PolygonComplex2D (merge_tol=0.15)" in dark grey.
    *   *Left side of inset:* Shows two nearly cocircular blue triangles sharing a diagonal blue edge. Inside each triangle is an orange dot representing the circumcentres. The two orange dots are almost touching, connected by a tiny, prominently red dual edge. A red label points to this edge reading, "short Voronoi dual edge shrinks 3D CFL timestep".
    *   *Center:* A dark grey arrow labeled "merge" points to the right.
    *   *Right side of inset:* Shows the result of the merge—a single, clean quadrilateral outlined in blue, containing a single central orange dot (dual vertex) with a bright green checkmark placed next to it.
*   **Bottom Note:** At the very bottom of the left panel, written in dark grey text: "220 nm Si micro-ring: 15× fewer unknowns, 22× less work than Cart.; ~28× faster in wall time than 3D tets on rod cavity".

**Right Panel: 3D Tetrahedral FIT (UnstructuredFIT3D)**
*   **Header:** Positioned at the top in large, bold, dark grey sans-serif text is "3D Tetrahedral FIT (UnstructuredFIT3D)".
*   **Top Half (Tetrahedron Schematic):** Displays a large, clear 3D tetrahedron. The primary edges are drawn as thin blue lines, with directional arrows placed along them and labeled with blue '$e$'s to represent electric voltages. One of the primal triangular faces of the tetrahedron is shaded with a light translucent blue fill and contains a blue '$b$' denoting magnetic flux. Piercing cleanly through the center of this shaded blue face is an orange line representing the dual edge.
*   **Bottom Half (Comparison Cards):** Contains two distinctly outlined rectangular cards comparing Hodge methodologies.
    *   *Card 1 (Left/Top):* Titled in dark grey `hodge="voronoi"`. The descriptive text reads: "diagonal Delaunay–Voronoi Hodge, explicit leapfrog (52 ns/tet/step)". Below the text is a red warning sketch illustrating a flattened "sliver" tetrahedron drawn with thin red lines, with its corresponding orange circumcentre dot sitting clearly *outside* the boundaries of the tetrahedral volume. A red label next to it reads: "sliver tetrahedron: negative dual entries".
    *   *Card 2 (Right/Bottom):* Titled in dark grey `hodge="whitney" (Bossavit & Kettunen 1999)`. The descriptive text reads: "consistent non-diagonal Whitney 1-form / 2-form mass matrices, unconditionally SPD on slivers (sparse LU via splu, $O(N_{\text{tet}}^{1.5})$ memory)". (No additional geometric drawing is inside this second card, keeping it text-focused).
